summary: ObjectGenome validates supportKeys as an acyclic externally reachable construction/load graph but never proves that a supported component physically contacts its referenced support in the authored reference pose. The office-table top can be redirected only to the crossbar, leaving a 0.09 m vertical gap while the graph remains valid and ground-reachable.
evidence: Current ObjectGenome.inspect() checks support-key existence, self/duplicate edges, cycles, and fixed-point external-support reachability, but no support-edge geometry/contact predicate compares the linked components.

The shipped office-table top has bottom face y=0.28 m; its crossbar has top face y=0.19 m. Replacing only top.supportKeys with {crossbar} leaves a 0.09 m authored gap while retaining an acyclic top -> crossbar -> legs -> ground path.
Current component.outside_bounds validation checks each component independently against the object envelope and therefore cannot reject this disconnected support edge.
Issues/PR search surfaced #125 for deterministic graph reachability and #311/#352 for fixture-specific cart contact, but no generic ObjectGenome support-contact validator owner.
PRs #480, #489, and #466 own separate affordance-radius, caster-radius, and caster-axis locality/relation findings.
Docs/OBJECTGENOME_SUPPORT_CONTACT_GEOMETRY_FINDING.md records the bounded source-only finding; no production behavior or Studio/physical-contact evidence is changed or claimed.

metadata.recommendedNext: When explicitly unlocked, define v1 support-edge authored-contact semantics, add an expected-red disconnected office-table support regression, and apply the smallest deterministic rotated-bounds/tolerance rule that preserves existing fixtures and graph diagnostics.
